signoff.notes: The reviewer explicitly approved event-level signoff after reviewing the final event summary and Q1-Q7 judgments: eleven positive facts (four mapped command observations, four electrical differences, two same-mapped-asset capture-time relations, and one observation-channel asset mapping) plus six independent guardrails. Source and formatting checks passed. The administrative guardrail keys, support-set production availability accounting, signed-difference wording correction, and whitespace correction are documented separately in the closeout audit. Captured requests, reported values, and temporal relations do not establish execution, physical causation, malicious intent, compromise, or attacker identity. Q6 remains insufficient in all views; this does not establish safety. This completes single-reviewer development-pilot annotation only, not second-reviewer adjudication, formal gold publication, system evaluation, or protocol freeze.

question_review.notes: Q1 is answerable from N and EN because four distinct mapped command requests are retained as salient human-reviewed network facts. E-only does not contain network evidence and is therefore insufficient. The communication-gap candidate was reviewed but not selected as salient gold.

Q2 is answerable from E and EN because four salient human-reviewed electrical-change facts are supported by valid before/after E evidence, covering current, voltage, active power, and reactive power. N-only does not expose electrical/process values and is therefore insufficient. The gold set is intentionally salient rather than exhaustive.

Q3 is answerable in E from an observed electrical/process record plus its approved channel-to-asset mapping, and in N from the four human-reviewed command-address-to-control-point/asset mappings. EN contains both forms of supported asset/channel relationship.

Q4 is answerable in E because supported electrical observations provide distinct capture times, and in N because four mapped command requests occur at distinct capture times. EN supports both single-domain timelines and the retained cross-domain same-asset temporal associations. Capture-time ordering does not establish device action time or causation.

Q5 requires both supported network activity and supported electrical/process observations with a defensible capture-time relationship. E-only and N-only each lack one side of the cross-domain relation. EN supports multiple same-mapped-asset temporal associations; under the frozen two-temporal-fact salience cap, the retained representatives are the minimum-|delta_t| relation g_0003 and maximum-|delta_t| relation g_0013. Other valid temporal candidates remain excluded for benchmark salience only. Capture-time ordering does not establish execution or physical causation.

No reviewed observation in this event supports a positive review_required security interpretation. Salient command, electrical, and temporal observations remain event-reconstruction facts and are not automatically security indicators.

Q7 is answerable in E, N, and EN because each view permits supported statements about the limits of what can be concluded from its visible evidence. The retained guardrails cover insufficient support for command execution, physical causation, malicious intent, successful compromise, attacker identity, and benign/safe conclusions from absence of evidence. Question-level support means the limitations can be identified; it does not mean the prohibited stronger propositions themselves are supported.
